officials.name: Liz Breadon
officials.address: 1 City Hall Square Room 550 Boston, MA 02201-2043 United States
officials.bio: First elected in 2020, Liz Breadon is serving her fourth term as District 9 City Councilor, and is honored to represent all residents of Allston-Brighton at City Hall. In 2026, Councilor Breadon was elected as Boston City Council President. She is the first openly LGBTQ+ woman elected to the Boston City Council, the first openly LGBTQ+ woman to serve as Boston City Council President, and the first Council President to represent Allston-Brighton.

officials.name: Brian Worrell
officials.address: 1 City Hall Square Room 550 Boston, MA 02201-2043 United States
officials.bio: Brian Worrell is the Boston City Councilor for District 4, which includes Mattapan, Dorchester, and parts of Jamaica Plain and Roslindale. He has served as Vice President of the Boston City Council and Chair of the Council’s Committee on Ways and Means, where he led the Council’s review of the City’s FY25 and FY26 budgets. A native Bostonian, Councilor Worrell is the son of parents who immigrated from Jamaica and Barbados and is a small business owner.

officials.name: Edward M. Flynn
officials.address: 1 City Hall Square Room 550 Boston, MA 02201-2043 United States
officials.bio: In January 2022, Councilor Edward M. Flynn was unanimously elected by his colleagues to serve as Council President. A resident of District 2, he previously served as a Probation Officer and for 24 years in the U.S. Navy and U.S. Navy reserve, including Operation ENDURING FREEDOM. He also worked for five years in the U.S. Department of Labor under President Clinton.

officials.name: Enrique J. Pepén
officials.address: 1 City Hall Square Room 550 Boston, MA 02201-2043 United States
officials.bio: Enrique J. Pepén is the Boston City Councilor for District 5, representing Hyde Park, Mattapan, Readville, and Roslindale, and is entering his second term. He is a solutions-driven leader focused on transportation safety, housing affordability, immigrant protections, and responsive constituent services. Born and raised in Boston, he is the proud son of two Dominican immigrants.

officials.name: Erin J. Murphy
officials.address: 1 City Hall Square Room 550 Boston, MA 02201-2043 United States
officials.bio: Erin J. Murphy is a Boston City Councilor At-Large and a dedicated public servant, currently serving her third full term on the Council. Prior to her election, she spent over two decades as a teacher in Boston Public Schools. Councilor Murphy is a strong advocate for public health, recovery, and effective city governance, focusing on education, housing, and public safety.

officials.name: Gabriela Coletta Zapata
officials.address: 1 City Hall Square Room 550 Boston, MA 02201-2043 United States
officials.bio: Fighting on behalf of her community is the only thing Councilor Gabriela “Gigi” Coletta Zapata has ever known. Raised by community advocates in East Boston, Councilor Coletta Zapata grew up attending civic association meetings, neighborhood events, and even multiple protests against airport runway expansion alongside her mother, Nina. Those early experiences shaped a lifelong commitment to advocacy, equity, and public service — a commitment she has carried into every stage of her career and leadership on the Boston City Council.

officials.name: Henry Santana
officials.address: 1 City Hall Square Room 550 Boston, MA 02201-2043 United States
officials.bio: Henry Santana, an At-Large City Councilor, brings a unique blend of experiences and a deep commitment to community upliftment, having grown up in Mission Hill after moving to Boston from the Dominican Republic. Dedicated to community service from a young age, he previously served as the inaugural director for Mayor Michelle Wu's Office of Civic Organizing and as Director of Operations for Councilor Kenzie Bok. Councilor Santana is committed to representing every resident of Boston and creating a more accessible and equitable city.

officials.name: John FitzGerald
officials.address: 1 City Hall Square Room 550 Boston, MA 02201-2043 United States
officials.bio: John FitzGerald was elected to the Boston City Council on November 7, 2023, representing District 3 which includes most of Dorchester and a portion of the South End. He grew up in a tight-knit Boston family where serving others was an important value, and has a long history of public service with the City of Boston.

officials.name: Julia M. Mejia
officials.address: 1 City Hall Square Room 550 Boston, MA 02201-2043 United States
officials.bio: Boston City Councilor At-Large Julia Mejia is a trailblazer and a dedicated community advocate. Making history in 2019 by winning her first term with a single vote, she became the first Afro-Latina to hold a seat on the Boston City Council. In her fourth term as a City Councilor At-Large, Councilor Mejia is a proven barrier breaker, independent voice, and someone who speaks truth to power while creating space for others to step into their power.

officials.name: Miniard Culpepper
officials.address: 1 City Hall Square Room 550 Boston, MA 02201-2043 United States

officials.name: Ruthzee Louijeune
officials.address: 1 City Hall Square Room 550 Boston, MA 02201-2043 United States
officials.bio: Ruthzee Louijeune, serving her third term as City Councilor At-Large, is a grounded, thoughtful, and inclusive leader. A dedicated public servant, Councilor Louijeune is committed to fostering shared prosperity in Boston with a focus on justice and equity. Born and raised in Mattapan and Hyde Park to working-class Haitian immigrants, Councilor Louijeune's journey is deeply rooted in the fabric of Boston.

officials.name: Brandon Ward
officials.bio: Brandon Ward serves as the District 2 City Councilor for Precincts 25, 26, and 27. He is also the Executive Director of Leadership MetroWest.

officials.name: Christine A. Long
officials.bio: Christine A. Long serves as the District 1 City Councilor for Framingham, representing Precincts 22, 23, and 24. She chairs the Planning & Zoning Subcommittee and is Vice Chair of the Public Health, Safety, Transportation and Rules, Ordinances and Ethics Subcommittees. Her municipal experience includes serving on the Planning Board and Zoning Board of Appeals, and she is a founding member of the former Community Outreach Project.

officials.name: George King
officials.bio: George P. King, Jr. serves as City Council Chair & Councilor-at-Large for Framingham, MA. He is an attorney and is married to Allison Potter with two daughters. He holds degrees from Boston College, Framingham State University, and Massachusetts School of Law.

officials.name: Janet Leombruno
officials.bio: Janet Leombruno serves as the City Council Vice Chair and Councilor-at-Large for Framingham, MA. She chairs the Appointment Subcommittee and is Vice Chair for Education, Library, Arts and Culture, Elder and Veteran Services. Her extensive municipal experience includes serving as a former Town Meeting Member and Framingham Charter Commissioner.

officials.name: John Stefanini
officials.bio: John Stefanini is the District 8 City Councilor (Precincts 4, 5, 6) and an attorney. He is married to Cecilia and has two daughters and a Labrador Retriever named Ellie.

officials.name: Leora Mallach
officials.bio: Leora Mallach is an entrepreneur who holds a BA in Anthropology from Washington University in St. Louis and a Masters in Education from the University of Vermont.

officials.name: Mary Kate Feeney
officials.bio: Mary Kate Feeney is the District 3 City Councilor for Framingham, MA, serving on the Rules Ordinances & Ethics Subcommittee and as Vice Chair of the Environment & Sustainability Subcommittee. She is a small business owner with a background in political science and history, and is actively involved in various community organizations.

officials.bio: Michael P. Cannon is currently serving his fourth term on the Framingham City Council, a role he has held since Framingham became a City on January 1, 2018. He has served on various subcommittees and is actively involved in issues and organizations supporting small business, economic development, seniors, veterans, the arts, animal welfare, parks and open space, education, as well as food insecurity and hunger.

officials.bio: Noval Alexander is a retired U.S. Army Reservist and current teacher aide. He holds a B.A. in Government from The University of Texas at Austin and has served as a District 5 School Committee member and is currently a Commissioner for the Massachusetts Citizens Commission.

officials.name: Philip R. Ottaviani, Jr
officials.bio: Philip R. Ottaviani, Jr. is the District 6 City Councilor (Precincts 7, 8, 9). He is a small business owner and local realtor, married to Valerie, a Critical Care Nurse, and has a daughter, Julia.

The Mayor is the Chairman of the School Committee.

officials.bio: Joseph M. Petty is serving his fifteenth two-year term as Councilor-At-Large and his eighth term as Mayor of the City of Worcester, also serving as Chairman of the Worcester School Committee. He has been Mayor since January 2012 and holds a BS in Business Administration from Nichols College and a law degree from New England School of Law. Mayor Petty prioritizes reliable police and fire services, budgetary prudence, and improving infrastructure in schools and neighborhoods.
